Matt — appreciate the clear asks. I pulled together a first-pass MAP draft and two capacity sizing scenarios (attached PDF). High-level callouts:

1) Leadtimes: H100 private deployment (VPC + dedicated runtime) typical onboarding 6–8 weeks from contract execution if we have SOC2 evidence and procurement is straightforward; A100 path can be 4–6 weeks with faster kernel tuning but slightly higher per-token cost.

2) Sizing scenarios: we modeled three buckets — conservative (1.2B tokens/mo baseline), growth (2.5B), and burst (4.0B) — with recommended reserved GPU tranches. For your stated workloads, we recommend starting with a 4-GPU tranche (H100-80GB equiv) with a 20% staging buffer.

3) MAP milestones I propose:
   - Week 0: Sign MAP + NDA (if needed)
   - Week 1–2: SOC2 evidence exchange + network runbook review
   - Week 2–4: Provisioning & image bake, initial model artifacts upload (customer)
   - Week 4–6: Staging load tests + quantization tuning
   - Week 6–8: Production cutover + SLA activation

I'm copying Marissa and Karthik so we can get procurement and capacity planning aligned. Will you and procurement confirm target dates and any internal procurement windows?

Best,
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Looping in capacity ops + acceptance lead. Quick notes on execution risk and alternatives:

- If Crescent has strict procurement windows that push signature beyond 2 weeks, we should offer a 30-day soft-hold (no billing) to lock tranches while procurement completes; this protects both sides.
- Kernel tuning: H100 can save ~18% per-token on large-context models but requires an extra 7–10 day tuning window; plan that into the MAP if they need that efficiency.
- Acceptance criteria we need from Crescent for Private: list of IP allow/deny, test prompts, and a signed rollback SLA.

Action items for us: Karthik, can you run a reserve-availability check for the proposed 4-GPU H100 tranche for the 6–8 week window? Irene, I'll need a redline of terms (billing cadence & termination flexibility) to send to procurement.

-Marissa
